ClientResponses.Response:
We are very sorry to hear about the gas issues you are describing. This is not the norm! We reached out to you via email because it sounds like there is a leak at your propane tank. The low temperatures you described also indicate the leak-safety mechanism in your grill has been triggered. We are recommending a leak test before grilling again as well as always shutting off the propane tank at the end of every grilling session. 
Once your gas is flowing correctly through the grill, you should not have any further heat issues with searing steaks or burgers. Please reply to our email so we can get you grilling at full temperature soon!
ClientResponses.Name: Weber Grills

Results.ReviewText: I'm surprised how little use of this grill it takes to go from full propane tank to not empty but unusable due to low tank pressure - and the tank-fullness scale absolutely does not work -- it sticks at any given point, and by agitating the tank on the hanger, you can get it to register full, empty, or anything in between, regardless of whether it's actually full or empty.  I have looked online to see how to convert it to natural gas, as running out to get more propane after every 2 or so meals is very inconvenient (and expensive).  It is also disappointing that it never gets hot enough to really sear a steak, though with a full propane tank, the steaks come out quite good.  Burgers are a different story - they either fail to cook properly on the outside (with the hood open) or they bake through like a meat loaf (with the hood closed).
Results.Title: I'm not really satisfied with this product

Results.ReviewText: Assembly was fine, grill heats up fast and cooks well.  One complaint:  whereas I could easily roll my old Weber Silver on its four caster wheels, this one replaces two of the wheels with posts, so you have to lift the end to move it.  Instead of a handle to lift, it has a fold-out shelf.  If the shelf is collapsed (e.g., to make it easier to put on the cloth cover), you can't easily move the grill; if the shelf is extended, the act of using it as a handle puts stress on the folding joint. Better design would have been to put four wheels on the grill, just like the old ones.  Two caster wheels would cost a couple of bucks ... ?
Results.Title: Bring back the wheels
